name: Cholera & mosquito-borne
summary: Cholera deaths continue in DR Congo, with insecurity limiting access in the east; DRC leads new deaths globally
state: ECDC's monthly update of 27 Oct counts 291,272 cholera cases and 2,471 deaths worldwide in 2026, with DR Congo reporting the most new deaths, 288. WHO counted over 125,000 suspected cases and 3,644 deaths in DR Congo from January 2025 to September 2026, with 2,932 cases and 86 deaths in the week of 21–28 Sep; insecurity in the east limits access for medical teams (Ver Angola, citing WHO, 15 Oct). Searches on 8 Nov found no newer WHO count.
for_you: The worst effects are in conflict-affected areas with poor water and sanitation. Travellers can check FCDO travel advice and NHS Fit for Travel guidance.
rubric_hit: Alert: large outbreak with high mortality in a conflict zone (DR Congo, 3,644 suspected deaths since Jan 2025; access limited in the east)

sources.title: Ver Angola — WHO warns of over 125,000 suspected cases and 3,644 cholera deaths in DR Congo since 2025

why: Climate-sensitive diseases — cholera, dengue, chikungunya, Oropouche, West Nile and yellow fever — are hitting record levels and reaching new regions.
drivers: Conflict, floods, heat, El Niño, water and sanitation, mosquito range expansion.

rubric.alert: Large outbreaks with high mortality in conflict zones, or a WHO grade 3 emergency.
rubric.watch: Record-level seasons, or local transmission in countries where the disease was not established (including Europe).
